newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Former Philippine war zone attracts investors.
newsitem.headline: Former Philippine war zone attracts investors.

text.p: Businessmen have agreed to invest about $75 million in projects ranging from liquor manufacture to cattle fattening in a southern Philippine region now governed by former Moslem rebel chief Nur Misuari, officials on Tuesday.

The Indonesian company Kondur Petroleum and a local shipping firm have also expressed interest in setting up regular passenger and cargo services between Indonesia and the Philippines' southern islands, the presidential palace said in a statement.

It said the agreements reflected confidence by Filipino and foreign businessmen in Misuari, whom President Fidel Ramos installed on Monday as governor of a semi-autonomous four-province Moslem region.

Business deals concluded at Misuari's inauguration included the construction of a one billion peso ($38 million) commercial complex in Cotabato city and the allocation of 780 million pesos loanable funds by the Philippine National Bank for poor communities, the statement said.

Other deals include supply of raw materials for the Manila liquour firm La Tondena distillery, expansion of pineapple, corn and vegetable production, telecommunications, poultry and cattle fattening, it added.
The semi-autonomous region comprises the provinces of Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi, which are regarded as among the poorest areas in the country.
Misuari last month signed a peace deal with Manila ending a 24-year Moslem separatist revolt that killed more than 120,000 people.
The accord also calls for creation of a council to oversee development in 14 southern provinces prior to the establishment of an expanded autonomy area three years later.
